content: The Vaccines for Children (VFC) program has been instrumental in protecting children from preventable diseases for the past 30 years. Vaccines have been saving lives for over a century and remain critical in safeguarding individuals from life-threatening illnesses. The VFC program ensures that all eligible children in the United States have access to vaccinations against 19 different diseases at no cost. This initiative has significantly contributed to public health by reducing the prevalence of vaccine-preventable diseases among children. The latest issue of the CDC's Vital Signs report provides detailed insights into the successes of the VFC program and highlights areas where improvements are still needed. For those interested in a deeper understanding, the full report is available in the Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report (MMWR). Additionally, an American Sign Language (ASL) video is available for accessibility. The CDC Vital Signs reports focus on critical health threats and outline actionable steps to mitigate these risks. Individuals can subscribe to email updates to stay informed about the latest Vital Signs reports. The CDC also offers content syndication services, allowing organizations to integrate Vital Signs content into their websites. For those seeking historical information, archived content is available through the CDC's archive site. However, it is important to note that archived materials are no longer updated and may contain outdated information. The most recent update to this content was made on August 13, 2024, by the Office of the Associate Director for Communication.
